findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/NonsingularInverse.lean:189 `@[simp, norm_cast] theorem coe_units_inv (A : (Matrix n n α)ˣ) : ↑A⁻¹ = (A⁻¹ : Matrix n n α)`; TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/UpperUnitriangular.lean:48-50 `@[simp] IsUpperUnitriangular.coe_toGL`; `GL n R` is an `abbrev` for `(Matrix n n R)ˣ` (mathlib .../GeneralLinearGroup/Defs.lean:43). Contrast GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean:268 `(localizedGenericMatrix R n).map (antipode R n) = (localizedGenericMatrix R n)⁻¹`.
findings.fix: State the antipode RHS as `(genericMatrix R m)⁻¹` (Mathlib's nonsingular inverse), as the merged `GeneralLinear.map_antipode_localizedGenericMatrix` does; the bridge is `Matrix.coe_units_inv` plus `IsUpperUnitriangular.coe_toGL`.
findings.issue: All five public antipode lemmas (`map_antipode_genericMatrix` 256, `antipode_genericMatrix_apply` 273, `antipode_X` 281, `coordinateHopfAlgebra_antipode_X` 437, `coordinateHopfAlgebra_antipode_genericMatrix_apply` 447) state the RHS as `↑((isUpperUnitriangular_genericMatrix R m).toGL⁻¹)`, which is not simp-normal: `Matrix.coe_units_inv` (`@[simp, norm_cast]`) then `Matrix.IsUpperUnitriangular.coe_toGL` (`@[simp]`) rewrite it to `(genericMatrix R m)⁻¹`. These `@[simp]` lemmas therefore produce terms simp immediately rewrites further, goals normalized by `simp` no longer match them for `rw ←`, and Mathlib's `Matrix.inv` API (`mul_nonsing_inv`, `inv_apply`, `IsUpperUnitriangular.inv`) does not attach to the stated form.

findings.evidence: grep of `IsUpperUnitriangular` across TauCeti shows Triangular.lean has `isUpperUnitriangular_def`, `.apply_diag`, `.mul`, `.inv`, `.map` but no extensionality lemma, and `UpperUnitriangular.lean:75-157` (namespace `UpperUnitriangularGroup`) has none either; the new file's own three public consumers (lines 563, 573, 584, 622) all go through the private version.
findings.fix: Make both public alongside the API they extend: the matrix version in `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Triangular.lean` (as `Matrix.IsUpperUnitriangular.ext`-style, matching `IsUpperUnitriangular.mul`/`.inv`), the group version as `TauCeti.UpperUnitriangularGroup.ext` in `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/UpperUnitriangular.lean`; both files are already imported.
findings.issue: `matrix_eq_of_isUpperUnitriangular_of_apply_of_lt` (98) and `upperUnitriangularGroup_ext_of_lt` (488) are private, yet they are the extensionality principle for `Matrix.IsUpperUnitriangular`/`upperUnitriangularGroup`, which exists nowhere else in the repo. The only public characterization of the exposed `pointToUpperUnitriangular`/`pointsMulEquiv` is on strict-upper entries (`pointToUpperUnitriangular_apply_of_lt`), so no downstream file can conclude equality of two points or identify a point's matrix without re-deriving these lemmas.

findings.evidence: GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean:263 and :270; SplitTorus/Basic.lean:119,127; RootsOfUnity/Basic.lean:140,226; AdditiveGroup/Basic.lean:31. `GeneralLinear.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue` is consumed downstream at SpecialLinear/Basic.lean:487, and `pointsNatIso` (GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean:344-351) is built from it.
findings.fix: Add `pointsMulEquiv_mapValue` and `mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply` (both one-liners from `pointToUpperUnitriangular_mapValue` plus `pointsMulEquiv_apply` and injectivity), mirroring `GeneralLinear.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue`.
findings.issue: Naturality is stated only for the unbundled `pointToUpperUnitriangular`; the packaged `pointsMulEquiv` has neither `pointsMulEquiv_mapValue` nor `mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply`, and there is no naturality statement for `upperUnitriangularToPoint`. Every other points module in the repo provides both, and the natural isomorphism the module doc defers to is built from exactly `pointsMulEquiv_mapValue`.

summary: The Hopf-algebra surface mirrors the merged GL coordinate ring correctly, but three interface defects remain: the antipode's characteristic lemmas are stated off Mathlib's simp normal form for matrix inverses, the extensionality principle every consumer of the point maps needs is private, and the naturality lemmas for the exposed `pointsMulEquiv` (present in every other points module) are missing.
